content.thinking:
Now I see the issue. In `getToolInputDisplay`, when `result.toolInput` has a single entry and its value is an array of objects (like the todo items for TodoWrite), it does `String(entries[0][1])` which converts the array to a string. When you call `String()` on an array of objects, each object gets `.toString()` called on it, producing `[object Object]`.

For example, if the TodoWrite tool input is something like:
```json
{
  "todos": [
    { "id": 1, "task": "..." },
    { "id": 2, "task": "..." },
    ...
  ]
}
```

Then `entries` would be `[["todos", [{...}, {...}, ...]]]`, and `String(entries[0][1])` would produce `[object Object],[object Object],...`.

The fix is to update `getToolInputDisplay` to check if the single-value input is an object or array, and if so, use `JSON.stringify()` instead of `String()` to properly serialize it.

content.text:
Found the bug. In `getToolInputDisplay` at line 28 of `InlineQueryResult.tsx`:

```ts
if (entries.length === 1) return String(entries[0][1]);
```

When a tool like TodoWrite has a single input whose value is an array of objects, `String(arrayOfObjects)` calls `.toString()` on each object, producing `[object Object]`. The fix is to JSON.stringify non-primitive values.
